title: Begrüßungen und die Bäckerei
summary: Greetings by time of day, bitte and danke, and your first exchange at the bakery

blocks.title: Hello, by the clock
blocks.body: German greets you by the time of day. *Guten Morgen* in the morning, *Guten Tag* through the day, *Guten Abend* in the evening. **Hallo** works any time and is friendly; **Moin** is the northern hello you'll hear all over Berlin and Hamburg — morning or not. To leave: **Tschüss** (casual) or **Auf Wiedersehen** (formal).

blocks.title: bitte and danke — the whole engine
blocks.body: **danke** is thanks; *danke schön* and *vielen Dank* are "thank you very much". **bitte** is the Swiss-army word: it means **please**, **you're welcome**, and **here you go** — all decided by context. Miss a word? *Entschuldigung* (excuse me / sorry) opens every door.
blocks.callout: Say *bitte* when you ask, and *bitte* again when you hand something over.

pairs.note: Use the formal pair with strangers, officials, and older people. Tomorrow: the du/Sie system underneath this.

blocks.prompt: You walk into the Bäckerei at 8 a.m. Which greeting fits?
blocks.explain: *Guten Morgen* — morning. *Guten Abend* is evening; *Gute Nacht* is only for going to bed.

blocks.scene: Your first morning at the Bäckerei. Lena goes first and shows you how it's done.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Guten Morgen. Und für mich einen Kaffee, bitte.
lines.en: Good morning. And a coffee for me, please.
lines.spotlight: *bitte* closes almost every order — polite and effortless.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.spotlight: *Tschüss* is the everyday bye; *bis morgen* = see you tomorrow.
